lines.note: CORRECTED — previous agent marked all 8 words bold; I read NO word on this line as bold. Two findings. (1) The line is homogeneous: every glyph that repeats across words has the same ink area — e '1212/1233/1219' (The/warmongers/sure.), n '688/707,705/700' (warmongers/mining/bitcoin), r '635,645/640/612/607' (warmongers/start/for/sure.), i '930/940,951/933' (will/mining/bitcoin), o '675/666', s '844/831/827', w '1331/1320', m '1548/1522', a '796/781', g '973/955'. A side-by-side montage of the three e's, three n's, three r's and three i's shows them pixel-for-pixel alike. So the 'The/will/mining/bitcoin/sure. are heavy, warmongers/start/for are light' impression is purely the narrow-stem-letter artifact: in this display face the stem letters (T h e w m i l u b f) print fat and the round letters (a c o n r s t g) print thin, WITHIN single words — 'warmongers' has fat w/m/e and thin a/r/o/n/g/s, 'mining' has fat m/i/i and thin n/n/g. (2) The line's weight register is NOT the body bold. Scaling 'bitcoin' from bold line 16 to the same x-height and overlaying makes line 19's c/o/n/t visibly thinner. Numerically line 19's n = sw 4.2 at h39; scaled from the regular body n (3.55 at h31) predicts 4.47, scaled from the bold body n (4.83) predicts 6.08. Same for o (4.23 actual vs 4.65 regular-predicted / 6.83 bold-predicted), a, c, r, s. Whole-line x-height ratio is 0.123 versus 0.117 regular and 0.157-0.167 bold. I therefore record all 8 words as REGULAR. The five stem-heavy words are flagged uncertain because they read as bold to the eye and because this display face's relative letter weights match neither body face exactly (its 'e' counter is filled shut) — but whatever the answer is, it must be the SAME for all 8 words.

For contrast, the genuinely bold line 25 has n=4.6-4.7 and a=4.4-4.9. Whole line REGULAR. Note this line is set ~12% larger than lines 24-25, which is why its regular strokes still out-measure them.
